situation:
You are the marketing director at PEARWOOD CINEMAS, a four-theater movie chain run by the same family in the same river valley for three generations. The owner (judge) is the third generation to run it. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how the chain should handle this year's film club renewals and what a membership ought to cost.

The chain's downtown flagship sells an annual film club membership. A member keeps one reserved seat for the Thursday evening classic series, and the family has promised for three generations that a member keeps that seat as long as they renew. The club is why much of the valley still drives past two newer multiplexes to sit in a building the owner's grandfather opened.

The flagship auditorium reopened this spring after a renovation that pulled out its old rows and put in wide recliners. It now holds 210 recliners where it once held 380 seats. Renewal notices went out in March and came back from far more members than the room can now seat, and no one in the family has ever had to tell a member that the seat is gone.

One path is to renew every current member at the price they pay now and close the club to new members, which keeps the promise but tells the younger valley moviegoers the chain has been trying to reach that there is no room for them. The other is to raise the renewal price until the requests fit the 210 recliners, which prices out long-standing members who have held the same Thursday seat for years.

The owner (judge) wants your recommendation on who the film club is for, what a renewal ought to cost, and how the chain says what it stands for to the members it cannot seat. The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.

You are the owner (judge) of PEARWOOD CINEMAS, a four-theater movie chain run by the same family in the same river valley for three generations. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You want the marketing director to tell you who the film club is for now that the flagship auditorium seats fewer people than it did, to recommend what a renewal ought to cost, and to say how the chain explains what it stands for to the members it cannot seat.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Which path did you decide against?
